parsed.explanation: The dossier documents no traveller-facing exposure: no trans-specific criminal statute, no documented police targeting, no facility restrictions, and no border/creening incidents. Extrapolating from structure (rule 13): a conservative society (12% marriage approval, strong religious opposition), no anti-discrimination or hate-crime protections, and stalled reforms mean that if a visitor is outed, recourse is thin and social reception uncertain outside the one accepting indigenous territory. Marriage and recognition fights are resident/LGB-facing and weigh little. The mix — latent hostility risk, thin recourse, no known enforcement against trans visitors — sits between the 0.45 and 0.55 anchors, resolved toward 0.55 because no exposure is documented beyond open questions.

entry_documents.exposure: Not documented. How border officers treat a passport marker differing from presentation is unknown (dossier flags this as an open question).
entry_documents.interaction: Possible document-check friction if outed; outcome unverifiable.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: No documented pattern of police targeting transgender people; no recorded detention cases.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: If detained, no hate-crime or anti-discrimination framework would apply.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: No statute on facility access by gender identity located; practice unknown.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Single-sex facilities governed by custom, not law; uncertain.

care_services.exposure: Gender recognition requires surgery and nonbinary recognition is absent — resident-facing; effect on visitors not documented. Blood-donation ban is resident-facing.
care_services.interaction: Visitor care access undocumented; no evidence of denial or acceptance.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: No explicit trans criminalisation; religious institutions strongly oppose LGBT recognition ('danger to the human race'), a hostility climate signal, not documented state targeting of trans people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Morally hostile climate could licence social hostility if outed.

minors_guardians.interaction: No child-specific rules in the dossier.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No hate-crime recognition means anti-trans violence is not recorded or charged as such; no documented pattern of such violence located.
street_violence_police_response.protection: General criminal law applies; no documented failure to protect trans victims.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Victims would lack identity-motivated charging recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination statute on SO/GI grounds; 2024 amendment blocked; 2015 bill stalled; hate-crime status absent — a visitor has essentially no statutory remedy.
remedies_unknowns.protection: General rule of law unassessed; UPR 2025 pressure noted.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies would run through generic courts only.

anchor_checks.comparison: Tarnov has documented universal-exposure gatekeeping (portal flagging, morality holds). This jurisdiction documents no such traveller-facing mechanism — only absence of protections and social conservatism — so it sits above 0.45-C.

Valdoria documents routine checkpoint stops and holding for document mismatches. Here no checkpoint practice is documented at all; the conservative social climate and thin remedies are comparable, but no operative exposure matches, placing this slightly above 0.55-A.
Vellmaris has working national equality law and courts that reliably order release after friction. This jurisdiction lacks any SO/GI remedy and has stalled reforms, so it sits clearly below 0.65-A.
Vellandra enforces a universal visitor register excluding trans entrants. Nothing comparable is documented here — no enforced traveller-facing restriction of any kind — so this sits well above 0.35.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is one of legal silence rather than active restriction: no trans-specific crime, no documented police or border targeting, no facility rules — but also no anti-discrimination, no hate-crime recourse, and a socially conservative, religiously opposed climate (12% regional approval of same-sex marriage), with one documented accepting indigenous enclave. A visitor who is outed faces uncertain social reception with only generic legal recourse; nothing in the record documents severe or organised consequences. Open questions (border handling, facilities, custody placement) are unresolved but not exposures. This places the jurisdiction moderately above the elevated-risk anchors and below the reduced-risk tier with working protections.
